gloss: reserve army; (figurative) at-risk group; pool of potential cases

definitions.explanation: Literally, military reserves — soldiers held back from active deployment but available if needed.

definitions.gloss: at-risk group; borderline cases; pool of potential X
definitions.explanation: Figurative and now far more common: a group of people not yet diagnosed or classified as X, but on track or at risk to become so. Standard in health and social-policy reporting.

examples.japanese: {予備軍|よびぐん}を{投入|とうにゅう}した。
{予備軍|よびぐん}の{兵士|へいし}が{招集|しょうしゅう}された。
{両国|りょうこく}は{緊張|きんちょう}{緩和|かんわ}のため、{予備軍|よびぐん}の{削減|さくげん}に{合意|ごうい}した。
examples.english: The two countries agreed to reduce their reserve forces to ease tensions.

examples.japanese: {糖尿病|とうにょうびょう}{予備軍|よびぐん}と{言|い}われた。
examples.english: I was told I'm at risk of becoming diabetic.

examples.japanese: {若者|わかもの}の{失業者|しつぎょうしゃ}{予備軍|よびぐん}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: The pool of young people at risk of unemployment is growing.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}{診断|しんだん}の{結果|けっか}、{高血圧|こうけつあつ}{予備軍|よびぐん}に{分類|ぶんるい}されたので{食事|しょくじ}に{気|き}をつけている。
examples.english: My checkup classified me as at risk for high blood pressure, so I'm watching my diet.

notes:
Compound of {予備|よび} (reserve/spare) + {軍|ぐん} (army/group). The figurative sense (sense 2) attaches to disease names, social categories, and economic statuses, naming a group not yet in the category but heading toward it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (sense 2):
- {糖尿病|とうにょうびょう}{予備軍|よびぐん}: pre-diabetic / at risk of diabetes
- {高血圧|こうけつあつ}{予備軍|よびぐん}: at risk of hypertension
- {認知症|にんちしょう}{予備軍|よびぐん}: at risk of dementia / MCI
- メタボ{予備軍|よびぐん}: at risk of metabolic syndrome
- ニート{予備軍|よびぐん}: at risk of becoming NEET

USAGE:
In medical writing, {予備軍|よびぐん} often corresponds to English 'pre-' prefixes (pre-diabetic, pre-hypertension) or 'at risk of'.
